Name: Supercharger load diagnosis - bypass command threshold
Comment: Threshold as a percentage of the 0-255 bypass command (raw * 100 / 255). Enables supercharger load diagnosis only when the bypass command exceeds this value. Setting 100% (raw 255) disables this diagnostic and its associated cutout, including genuine insufficient-load detection.
Fieldvalues.Name: Bypass command threshold

Name: Vehicle speed limiter
Comment: Vehicle-speed thresholds in km/h (stored unsigned 16-bit value / 16). Row and column indices start at 0. Column n is selected when (RAM[0x9C0C] & 7) = n: eight coding variants, not manual/automatic gearbox columns. All four rows use the same column, without interpolation between variants. Row 0: release threshold; at or below it, speed regulation is reset. Row 1: active-control update/recovery threshold. Row 2: entry threshold; above it, inactive speed regulation can start. Row 3: target speed used to calculate the regulation error. Original row 3 targets by column (km/h): 0=190, 1=210, 2=228, 3=242, 4=250, 5=250, 6=250, 7=250. If the vehicle-speed signal is invalid, row 3 also contributes to a fallback RPM ceiling through coding- and transmission-dependent conversion; it is not a fixed 5700 rpm limit.
Fieldvalues.Name: Vehicle speed

AxisY.Name: Control phase

Name: Camshaft adjustment
Comment: Packed command bits, not cam degrees. AT warm bits 0/1, AT cold 2/3, MT warm 4/5, MT cold 6/7. Prior OFF selects the lower bit, prior ON the upper. Pair 00=OFF, 10=hold, 11=ON, 01=toggles. No interpolation of states. Display uses RPM axis 0. Actual selector 8FD5.bits1:0 selects axes 0,1,2,3. RPM node addresses: 0x4c1b, 0x4c27, 0x4c33, 0x4c3f. Hexadecimal display in CSV, XDF and KP: FF=255, CF=207, EF=239. For MT warm only, FF to CF requests OFF, FF to EF holds, preserving other bits. ON/OFF denotes software command, not measured cam angle. Enable and diagnostic conditions still apply.

AxisY.Name: Throttle (normalized)

Comment: Upper MAF reading threshold for airflow plausibility diagnosis. If an excess is confirmed, the ECU can substitute measured airflow with the Engine Load Model. MAF [g/s] ~= corrected raw model byte x RPM x 0.00015561, including intake-air-temperature and learned adaptation corrections.
